what: Dante Controller's ARC 2.7 multicast flow create (0x2201) and delete (0x2202) to one of our devices, sent under start code 0x2809 while our 0x1000 states multicast TX (0x0020) and not segmented flows (0x1000): Device View > Transmit > Add, TX 1 and TX 2, Create; then the flow selected, Delete.
captured: 2026-11-12 05:22 CET, dstack #222 (`dc222a.pcapng`), pktmon on the Dante Controller PC, UDP to and from our test device (a lane build whose 0x1000 first word carried 0x0020 by a scratch override, not committed; it answered the create, showing "Multicast Flow 32: TX 1, TX 2", and refused the delete). The create here is dstack #220's from session a (`dc220a.pcapng`, sequence 0x00cd), refused then; this session's (sequence 0x00d2) holds the same bytes otherwise. Only our own device was written to. Nothing is changed: the frames hold no name and no address (a flow id, a channel count, channel numbers, offsets). netaudio 0.4.2's legacy encoders (`create_tx_flow` and `delete_tx_flow` family `fixed`, flow protocol 0x2729, flow 32, channels 1 and 2) write the same bodies under start code 0x2729.

layout.0x2201: body: [1, 1], the record's packet offset (0x0010), 0; the record: the flow id (its slot, from 1; Dante Controller picked 32), the flow type (2, multicast), the rate u32 (0: the device's), 0, the encoding (0: the device's), 0, the channel count, each slot's TX channel, the names block's packet offset, 0; the names block: 0x0a00, 0, 0, 0, frames per packet (0: the device's), the flow's label offset (0: none), 0, 0, 1, 0.
layout.0x2202: body: the count of flows (1), 0, then each flow id (32).
layout.answers: Dante Controller took the create's OK with no body and read the 2.7 list (0x2200) next, which listed the flow.
